# docker_service (Resource)

A Swarm service: a desired number of tasks (containers) of one image scheduled across the Swarm. Requires the provider to point at a Swarm manager. Almost every change is a rolling update in place (`ServiceUpdate`, governed by `update_config`); only `name` and changing `mode` (replicated, global, replicated_job, global_job) replace the service. Destroy removes the service and waits until its tasks are gone, so the networks, secrets and configs it used can be removed next. Add `converge_config {}` to make apply wait for the tasks to run.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "docker_secret" "db_password" {
  name = "db_password"
  data = base64encode("change-me")
}

resource "docker_config" "nginx" {
  name = "nginx-default.conf"
  data = base64encode("server { listen 80; location / { return 200 \"ok\n\"; } }")
}

resource "docker_service" "web" {
  name     = "web"
  image    = "nginx:1.27-alpine"
  replicas = 3

  # Overlay networks by name or ID, with extra DNS aliases per network.
  # (Use the plain `networks = ["frontend"]` set when no aliases are needed;
  # the two cannot be combined.)
  networks_advanced {
    name    = "frontend"
    aliases = ["www"]
  }

  env = {
    TZ = "UTC"
  }

  # Task container settings; all of these update in place (rolling update).
  hostname          = "web-{{.Task.Slot}}"
  user              = "nginx"
  hosts             = ["db.internal:10.0.0.5"]
  cap_drop          = ["NET_RAW"]
  sysctls           = { "net.core.somaxconn" = "1024" }
  stop_grace_period = "30s"

  dns {
    nameservers = ["10.0.0.2"]
    options     = ["ndots:2"]
  }

  ulimits {
    name = "nofile"
    soft = 65536
    hard = 65536
  }

  # Bump to force a rolling restart without other changes.
  force_update = 1

  labels = {
    app = "shop"
  }

  mounts {
    type   = "volume"
    source = "web-cache"
    target = "/var/cache/nginx"
  }

  endpoint_spec {
    ports {
      target_port    = 80
      published_port = 8080
    }
  }

  secrets {
    secret_id = docker_secret.db_password.id
    file_name = "db_password"
  }

  configs {
    config_id = docker_config.nginx.id
    file_name = "/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf"
  }

  update_config {
    parallelism    = 1
    delay          = "10s"
    failure_action = "rollback"
    order          = "start-first"
  }

  restart_policy {
    condition    = "on-failure"
    max_attempts = 3
  }

  placement {
    constraints = ["node.role==worker"]
    preferences = ["spread=node.labels.zone"]
  }

  resources {
    limits {
      nano_cpus    = 500000000
      memory_bytes = 268435456
    }
  }

  healthcheck {
    test     = ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "-O-", "http://localhost/"]
    interval = "30s"
    timeout  = "5s"
    retries  = 3
  }

  logging {
    driver = "json-file"
    options = {
      max-size = "10m"
    }
  }

  # Wait for all replicas to run before apply finishes.
  converge_config {
    timeout = "3m"
    delay   = "5s"
  }
}

# A one-off job: runs 6 tasks to completion, 2 at a time. With
# converge_config, apply waits until total_completions tasks completed.
# Changing mode (e.g. to "replicated") replaces the service.
resource "docker_service" "migrate" {
  name              = "db-migrate"
  image             = "busybox:1.36"
  args              = ["sh", "-c", "echo migrating; sleep 5"]
  mode              = "replicated_job"
  max_concurrent    = 2
  total_completions = 6

  restart_policy {
    condition = "on-failure"
  }

  converge_config {
    timeout = "5m"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `image` (String) Image reference the tasks run. The provider asks the registry for the digest and the daemon pins tasks to it (`@sha256:...`); that pin is ignored on refresh when this value has no digest. Credentials come from the provider's `registry_auth`. Updated in place (rolling update).
- `name` (String) Service name. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `args` (List of String) Arguments passed to the command (overrides the image `CMD`).
- `cap_add` (Set of String) Linux capabilities to add to the task containers, e.g. `NET_ADMIN` (case and `CAP_` prefix are ignored when comparing). Updated in place.
- `cap_drop` (Set of String) Linux capabilities to drop, e.g. `ALL`. Updated in place.
- `command` (List of String) Command to run (overrides the image `ENTRYPOINT`).
- `configs` (Block List) Swarm configs mounted as files in the task containers (default path `/run/secrets/<file_name>` for secrets, `/<file_name>` for configs). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--configs))
- `container_labels` (Map of String) Labels on the task containers.
- `converge_config` (Block, Optional) When present, create and update wait until the service has converged: the wanted number of tasks running (every desired task for `global`) and no update paused or rolling back; for `replicated_job`, `total_completions` tasks completed; for `global_job`, every task of the current run finished with at least one completed. On timeout the apply fails with the task errors. Not sent to the daemon. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--converge_config))
- `dir` (String) Working directory of the task process. Unset uses the image's. Updated in place.
- `dns` (Block, Optional) Resolver configuration of the task containers (`ContainerSpec.DNSConfig`). Updated in place. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--dns))
- `endpoint_spec` (Block, Optional) How the service is reached: resolution mode and published ports. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--endpoint_spec))
- `env` (Map of String) Environment variables of the task containers.
- `force_update` (Number) Counter (`TaskTemplate.ForceUpdate`): change it (e.g. increment) to force a rolling restart of every task even when nothing else changed, like `docker service update --force`. Unset leaves the daemon's counter alone and ignores it on refresh. Updated in place.
- `healthcheck` (Block, Optional) Container healthcheck; Swarm only counts healthy tasks as running. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--healthcheck))
- `hostname` (String) Hostname of the task containers (`ContainerSpec.Hostname`; Go templates such as `{{.Task.Name}}` work). Unset: the container ID prefix. Updated in place (rolling update).
- `hosts` (List of String) Extra `/etc/hosts` entries, each `"<hostname>:<ip>"` like `docker service create --host`. The provider sends them in the daemon's `"<ip> <hostname>"` (hosts(5)) format; an entry that already contains a space is sent as is. Updated in place.
- `labels` (Map of String) Labels on the service object.
- `logging` (Block, Optional) Log driver of the task containers. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--logging))
- `max_concurrent` (Number) `replicated_job` only: tasks run at the same time (daemon default 1). Updated in place (re-runs the job).
- `mode` (String) `replicated` (default; runs `replicas` tasks), `global` (one task per eligible node), `replicated_job` (runs `total_completions` tasks to completion, `max_concurrent` at a time) or `global_job` (one run-to-completion task per eligible node). The Engine API cannot change a service's mode type, so changing this forces replacement.
- `mounts` (Block List) Mounts in the task containers. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--mounts))
- `networks` (Set of String) Networks to attach the tasks to, by ID or name (resolved to IDs; overlay networks). In a stack, the short name of a stack `network` block resolves to `<stack>_<name>`. Use `networks_advanced` instead for per-network aliases; the two cannot be combined. Updated in place.
- `networks_advanced` (Block List) Networks to attach, with per-network DNS aliases (`TaskTemplate.Networks[].Aliases`). An alternative to `networks`: setting both is an error. Updated in place. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--networks_advanced))
- `placement` (Block, Optional) Where tasks may run. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--placement))
- `replicas` (Number) Number of tasks for `replicated` mode (default 1); ignored by the other modes. Updated in place.
- `resources` (Block, Optional) CPU and memory limits and reservations per task. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--resources))
- `restart_policy` (Block, Optional) When Swarm restarts tasks that exit. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--restart_policy))
- `rollback_config` (Block, Optional) How a failed update rolls back. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rollback_config))
- `secrets` (Block List) Swarm secrets mounted as files in the task containers (default path `/run/secrets/<file_name>` for secrets, `/<file_name>` for configs). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--secrets))
- `stop_grace_period` (String) Time to wait after the stop signal before killing a task (Go duration, e.g. `30s`; daemon default 10s). Updated in place.
- `sysctls` (Map of String) Namespaced kernel parameters for the task containers, e.g. `{ "net.core.somaxconn" = "1024" }`. Updated in place.
- `total_completions` (Number) `replicated_job` only: tasks that must complete successfully (daemon default: `max_concurrent`). Updated in place (re-runs the job).
- `ulimits` (Block List) Resource ulimits of the task containers. Updated in place. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--ulimits))
- `update_config` (Block, Optional) How a changed service rolls out to its tasks. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--update_config))
- `user` (String) User (`uid`, `name`, optionally `:group`) the task process runs as. Unset uses the image's. Updated in place.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The Swarm service ID.

<a id="nestedblock--configs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configs`

Required:

- `config_id` (String) ID or name of the config (resolved to its ID). In a stack, the short name of a stack `config` block resolves to `<stack>_<name>`.

Optional:

- `config_name` (String) Name of the config; looked up from the ID when unset.
- `file_name` (String) File name (or absolute path) in the container. Defaults to the reference as written when it is a name, otherwise the config name.
- `gid` (String) File group GID (default `0`).
- `mode` (Number) File mode as a decimal number (default `292`, i.e. `0444`).
- `uid` (String) File owner UID (default `0`).


<a id="nestedblock--converge_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `converge_config`

Optional:

- `delay` (String) Poll interval (Go duration, default `5s`).
- `timeout` (String) Maximum wait (Go duration, default `3m`).


<a id="nestedblock--dns"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dns`

Optional:

- `nameservers` (List of String) DNS server IPs.
- `options` (List of String) resolv.conf options, e.g. `ndots:2`.
- `search` (List of String) DNS search domains.


<a id="nestedblock--endpoint_spec"></a>
### Nested Schema for `endpoint_spec`

Optional:

- `mode` (String) `vip` (default, a virtual IP load-balances tasks) or `dnsrr` (DNS round robin).
- `ports` (Block List) Published ports. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--endpoint_spec--ports))

<a id="nestedblock--endpoint_spec--ports"></a>
### Nested Schema for `endpoint_spec.ports`

Required:

- `target_port` (Number) Port inside the tasks.

Optional:

- `protocol` (String) `tcp` (default), `udp` or `sctp`.
- `publish_mode` (String) `ingress` (default, routing mesh on every node) or `host` (only on nodes running a task).
- `published_port` (Number) Port published on the nodes. Unset lets Swarm choose one (30000+).



<a id="nestedblock--healthcheck"></a>
### Nested Schema for `healthcheck`

Optional:

- `interval` (String) Time between checks (Go duration).
- `retries` (Number) Consecutive failures before unhealthy.
- `start_period` (String) Start-up grace period (Go duration).
- `test` (List of String) Test command, e.g. `["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost/"]`, `["CMD-SHELL", "..."]` or `["NONE"]`.
- `timeout` (String) Time before a check counts as hung (Go duration).


<a id="nestedblock--logging"></a>
### Nested Schema for `logging`

Optional:

- `driver` (String) Log driver name, e.g. `json-file`.
- `options` (Map of String) Log driver options.


<a id="nestedblock--mounts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mounts`

Required:

- `target` (String) Path inside the container.
- `type` (String) `bind`, `volume` or `tmpfs`.

Optional:

- `read_only` (Boolean) Mount read-only.
- `source` (String) Host path (`bind`) or volume name (`volume`; created on each node by the volume driver if missing). In a stack, the short name of a stack `volume` block resolves to `<stack>_<name>` with that block's driver, options and labels.
- `tmpfs_size` (Number) Size of a `tmpfs` mount in bytes.
- `volume_driver` (String) Volume driver used when the volume does not exist yet on the node.
- `volume_driver_opts` (Map of String) Driver options for a volume created on first use.
- `volume_labels` (Map of String) Labels for a volume created on first use.


<a id="nestedblock--networks_advanced"></a>
### Nested Schema for `networks_advanced`

Required:

- `name` (String) Network ID or name (resolved to its ID). In a stack, the short name of a stack `network` block resolves to `<stack>_<name>`.

Optional:

- `aliases` (Set of String) Extra DNS names the service gets on this network (the service name always resolves).


<a id="nestedblock--placement"></a>
### Nested Schema for `placement`

Optional:

- `constraints` (List of String) Constraints such as `node.role==manager` or `node.labels.zone==a`.
- `max_replicas` (Number) Maximum tasks per node; 0 or unset means unlimited.
- `preferences` (List of String) Spread preferences, each `spread=<descriptor>` such as `spread=node.labels.zone`.


<a id="nestedblock--resources"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resources`

Optional:

- `limits` (Block, Optional) Hard limits. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--resources--limits))
- `reservations` (Block, Optional) Reservations the scheduler must find on a node. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--resources--reservations))

<a id="nestedblock--resources--limits"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resources.limits`

Optional:

- `memory_bytes` (Number) Memory in bytes.
- `nano_cpus` (Number) CPU in units of 1e-9 CPUs (1000000000 = one CPU).


<a id="nestedblock--resources--reservations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resources.reservations`

Optional:

- `memory_bytes` (Number) Memory in bytes.
- `nano_cpus` (Number) CPU in units of 1e-9 CPUs (1000000000 = one CPU).



<a id="nestedblock--restart_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `restart_policy`

Optional:

- `condition` (String) `none`, `on-failure` or `any` (default).
- `delay` (String) Delay between restart attempts (Go duration, e.g. `5s`).
- `max_attempts` (Number) Maximum restarts before giving up; 0 or unset means unlimited.
- `window` (String) Window used to evaluate the restart policy (Go duration).


<a id="nestedblock--rollback_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rollback_config`

Optional:

- `delay` (String) Delay between batches (Go duration).
- `failure_action` (String) `pause` (default), `continue` or `rollback`.
- `max_failure_ratio` (Number) Fraction of tasks that may fail before `failure_action` triggers (0 to 1).
- `monitor` (String) Time to watch each task for failure after it starts (Go duration).
- `order` (String) `stop-first` (default) or `start-first`.
- `parallelism` (Number) Tasks updated at once (default 1; 0 means all at once).


<a id="nestedblock--secrets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `secrets`

Required:

- `secret_id` (String) ID or name of the secret (resolved to its ID). In a stack, the short name of a stack `secret` block resolves to `<stack>_<name>`.

Optional:

- `file_name` (String) File name (or absolute path) in the container. Defaults to the reference as written when it is a name, otherwise the secret name.
- `gid` (String) File group GID (default `0`).
- `mode` (Number) File mode as a decimal number (default `292`, i.e. `0444`).
- `secret_name` (String) Name of the secret; looked up from the ID when unset.
- `uid` (String) File owner UID (default `0`).


<a id="nestedblock--ulimits"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ulimits`

Required:

- `hard` (Number) Hard limit.
- `name` (String) Ulimit name, e.g. `nofile`.
- `soft` (Number) Soft limit.


<a id="nestedblock--update_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `update_config`

Optional:

- `delay` (String) Delay between batches (Go duration).
- `failure_action` (String) `pause` (default), `continue` or `rollback`.
- `max_failure_ratio` (Number) Fraction of tasks that may fail before `failure_action` triggers (0 to 1).
- `monitor` (String) Time to watch each task for failure after it starts (Go duration).
- `order` (String) `stop-first` (default) or `start-first`.
- `parallelism` (Number) Tasks updated at once (default 1; 0 means all at once).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by service name or ID. Network references come back as IDs and the
# image with its digest pin until the configuration is applied once.
terraform import docker_service.web web
```
